assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, S3, and reset are encoded as discrete events because the text describes them as triggers/signals rather than persistent numeric variables.
hbrg is encoded as an integer output with 1 for upward drive, -1 for downward drive, and 0 for stop because the NL distinguishes three output conditions but does not specify numeric encodings.
The phrase 'immediately checks the next destination' is represented by request-triggered outgoing transitions from each floor state after arrival, not by additional unlisted decision states.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init verifies initial floor 1 stop, F1 PS2 upward travel to MU2, arrival at F2 stop, then immediate next request PS3 upward to MU3 and arrival at F3 stop
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_then_up_to_f2_and_f3

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from F1 verifies PS3 selects direct upward MU3 travel and S3 arrival stops at F3
scenario_results.name: f1_direct_request_to_f3

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from F2 verifies PS1 selects downward MD1 travel and S1 arrival returns to F1 stop
scenario_results.name: f2_request_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from F3 verifies PS2 selects downward MD2 travel and S2 arrival stops at F2
scenario_results.name: f3_request_down_to_f2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from F3 verifies PS1 selects downward MD1 travel and S1 arrival stops at F1
scenario_results.name: f3_request_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from an upward motion state verifies reset forces the controller back to floor 1 stop regardless of outstanding motion context
scenario_results.name: reset_forces_motion_state_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from a non-F1 floor state verifies reset forces the controller back to floor 1 stop regardless of outstanding request context
scenario_results.name: reset_forces_floor_state_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from F1 verifies that without any request or reset event the controller remains stopped on floor 1
scenario_results.name: no_request_stays_stopped_on_f1

evidence: NL: state space combines floor states F1, F2, and F3 with motion states MU2, MU3, MD1, and MD2.
DSL defines states F1, F2, F3, MU2, MU3, MD1, MD2.
NL: From F1, PS2 triggers MU2 and PS3 triggers MU3; DSL includes F1 -> MU2 :: PS2 and F1 -> MU3 :: PS3.
NL arrival transitions MU2 + S2 -> F2, MU3 + S3 -> F3, MD1 + S1 -> F1, MD2 + S2 -> F2 are all present in DSL.
DSL: ! * -> F1 :: reset implements reset forcing controller back to F1.
findings.summary: The DSL closely matches the NL-described elevator FSM: required floor states, motion states, request-triggered dispatch transitions, sensor-triggered arrival transitions, stop/up/down hbrg behavior, initial F1 state, and global reset to F1 are represented.

design_diagnostics_summary blocking_count = 0.
findings.summary: The model uses hbrg as a plain integer variable assigned in state entry actions; diagnostics warn it is unreferenced by guards. This is acceptable for a pure output but should remain documented as an output role rather than treated as control state.
